Original In order to bring transparency to moderators and their on-site activity, I thought about having an activity log for EVERY moderator action within the subverse. I also thought about having the private messages moderators send and receive be public, regardless of what is in it, but the issue of privacy rose up.

I haven't fleshed out the ideas, but yeah, you probably get the idea. On-site moderator activity transparency.

Edit As the Voat becomes larger, we have to take into account how we "watch the watchmen". For the activity logs, there will be the name of the mod and what they did, without specifics. For example, if a mod bans a user or deletes a post, the activity log will say something similar "Bluedonut1 deleted a post. Specified reason: Gore". Users can then request a detailed overview of what was deleted or the action the moderator took, with an archive link or something like that. However, there will be problems as we get bigger.

As for private messages, there should be a team of reviewers to edit out dox-able and illegal content like emails and addresses and child porn. The team should be under some sort of contract, so that dox information that does get released is punished through court.

EDIT: Fleshed out ideas and fixed grammatical errors.
Moderation Activity Log Tab and Moderator Transparency
At the very least have the option in a subverse' settings to make the moderation log public.

Ban logs being public and general transparency is a start, but if this place is going to subvert reddit's corruption then we need a direct way to keep administration/moderation in check. As it is, the moderation system is pretty similar to reddit's, and it's subject to the problems reddit has with its moderation as well, even if it'll be easier to spot these problems with elevated transparency. Having an exodus every time shoddy moderation is exposed and won't be dethroned can't go on forever.

I can't really say that foolproof implementations of this idea immediately come to mind, but I know we need to have a way to overthrow bad moderators.
It should be clear who was banned too and by who, and even better if posts are never deleted, unless is the most illegal thing, and if is that you could inquiry when there are too many of those

Two modes: Illegal and Unacceptable.

Mods choose one of those two options when deleting something. If the mods mark the post/comment Illegal, it gets thrown out completely after decaying for a few minutes. If they mark it Unacceptable, it shows up on the ModAcTab/Archive as having been downvoated to oblivion or upvoated to the heavens before it was removed.

A Casualty

 

That boy I took in the car last night,

With the body that awfully sagged away,

And the lips blood-crisped, and the eyes flame-bright,

And the poor hands folded and cold as clay --

Oh, I've thought and I've thought of him all the day.

 

For the weary old doctor says to me:

"He'll only last for an hour or so.

Both of his legs below the knee

Blown off by a bomb. . . . So, lad, go slow,

 

And please remember, he doesn't know."

So I tried to drive with never a jar;

And there was I cursing the road like mad,

When I hears a ghost of a voice from the car:

"Tell me, old chap, have I `copped it' bad?"

So I answers "No," and he says, "I'm glad."

 

"Glad," says he, "for at twenty-two

Life's so splendid, I hate to go.

There's so much good that a chap might do,

And I've fought from the start and I've suffered so.

'Twould be hard to get knocked out now, you know."

 

"Forget it," says I; then I drove awhile,

And I passed him a cheery word or two;

But he didn't answer for many a mile,

So just as the hospital hove in view,

Says I: "Is there nothing that I can do?"

 

Then he opens his eyes and he smiles at me;

And he takes my hand in his trembling hold;

"Thank you -- you're far too kind," says he:

"I'm awfully comfy -- stay . . . let's see:

I fancy my blanket's come unrolled --

My feet, please wrap 'em -- they're cold . . . they're cold."
